recommendation: Use the Container API path: publish the Python 3.12 FastAPI image to OCI Container Registry, run it as a persistent HTTP service on Container Instances, and expose port 8080 through API Gateway or a Load Balancer chosen after ingress and availability requirements are known. Start with a stateless smoke deployment using the existing /health endpoint, then add privately connected OCI Database with PostgreSQL after validating PostgreSQL version, extensions, pooling, migrations, backup/restore, HA, region availability, and cost. Do not start with OCI Functions because the repository uses a conventional persistent Uvicorn process, and do not use OKE unless Kubernetes requirements emerge. This is a planning-only, provisional recommendation; the next action is read-only confirmation of region, traffic pattern, public/private ingress, availability target, and PostgreSQL compatibility requirements.
aws_to_oci_mapping: AWS account and resource organization -> OCI tenancy plus a dedicated project compartment; compartments are access and governance boundaries, not separate billing accounts.
AWS ECS/Fargate or App Runner -> OCI Container Instances plus API Gateway or Load Balancer; this is an approximate mapping, not equivalent request autoscaling or scale-to-zero.
Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL -> OCI Database with PostgreSQL, subject to compatibility, private-connectivity, HA, backup, regional-availability, and cost validation.
AWS VPC -> OCI Virtual Cloud Network (VCN); use private subnets and Network Security Groups for the database.
AWS IAM task role -> OCI resource principal or other workload identity with narrowly scoped IAM policy; do not distribute user API keys.
AWS Secrets Manager and KMS -> OCI Vault keys and Secret Management.
Amazon CloudWatch -> OCI Logging, Monitoring, Alarms, and Notifications; telemetry and notification paths span multiple OCI services.
AWS Budgets -> OCI Budgets; alerts do not cap spending, while supported compartment quotas can enforce selected limits.
AWS CloudFormation/CDK -> OCI Terraform provider locally first, with OCI Resource Manager as a later execution option.
guardrails: Place workload resources in a dedicated project compartment, never the root compartment.
Keep the PostgreSQL endpoint private and restrict traffic with Network Security Groups.
Store database credentials in OCI Vault Secret Management; never commit secrets, embed them in images, or expose them in Terraform state or logs.
Grant workload identity only when the application needs OCI API access, using least-privilege policies; image pulling alone does not justify application credentials.
Validate current pricing, region availability, shapes, limits, quotas, and service capabilities against official OCI documentation before implementation because network verification was prohibited.
Create ownership and cost-attribution tags, a compartment-scoped budget alert, and supported quotas; a budget is an alert, not a spending cap.
Use Terraform as the canonical infrastructure description only if generation is later authorized; format, validate, preview, and obtain explicit approval immediately before any apply.
Plan logs, availability/error/latency metrics, alarms, monitored notifications, retention, and correlation identifiers before production exposure.
Record image digests, verification results, resource identifiers, rollback details, and exact teardown scope in a credential-free deployment receipt.
Do not claim production readiness from a single Container Instance; production requires explicit availability, scaling, replacement, and rollback decisions.
